rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.4 and 3.1-3.4 report the authors' own field measurements (sap-flow, eddy covariance, microlysimeters) in a super-intensive olive orchard in Alentejo, Portugal, 2011-2012, and their own SIMDualKc and METRIC (Landsat 5 TM / 7 ETM+) model runs compared with those measurements (Tables 3-5, Figs. 2-8).
rows.notes: The study is a primary ET/Kc estimation study. It shows that METRIC-derived ET and Kc from Landsat agree with ground-based ET (mean bias ~20% vs ETobs; Kc METRIC vs Kc SIMDualKc R2 = 0.86, b = 0.99) and that METRIC gives information on within-orchard spatial variability of ET. It does not test, measure or model any water management strategy, irrigation scheduling decision, water saving or water conservation outcome derived from the remote-sensing products. Applicability to irrigation management is only stated as a prospective use (Introduction: resulting information 'shall be later used to support improved irrigation management'; Conclusions: 'good perspectives' for using METRIC Kc as input to SIMDualKc). Thus the study supports only a precondition (accurate ET/Kc estimation) of the claimed water-conservation/fine-tuned water management effect; Q2 is 'no' and upstream is set. For completeness: the study does report limitations of its own ET/Kc results (small EC sample n = 28, n = 8 microlysimeter days, one-source model limitations for discontinuous canopies, need for longer time series) and SDs of ETMETRIC across pixels (0.19-0.82 mm/d), but these concern ET estimation, not water conservation, so Q8/Q9 remain 'no' under rule 3.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Single site (one 78 ha commercial orchard), one crop, two years; remote sensing component is METRIC applied to 16 Landsat images validated against sap-flow/EC-derived ET and SIMDualKc output.
